title: Backup Test Restore Success Rate
dataSources: Breach alerts (`hibp:alert`), password age snapshots (`passwordage:account`), backup restore tests (`backuprestore:test`), and DNS leak checks (`dnsleak:check`).
app: Personal security telemetry from Have I Been Pwned, password-age exports, backup restore drills, and DNS leak checks sent to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.

description: Tracks success rate for backup test restores by backup set. Runs scheduled SPL against `index=personal` to surface **Backup Test Restore Success Rate** so you can spot drift before it becomes a habit.
value: Restore success rate is more important than backup-job success because it proves the data can come back.
implementation: Capture explicit outcome states for backup test restores events in `index=personal` and review both attempts and success percentage over time.
visualization: Time chart of success percentage for backup test restores by backup set.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Personal Cyber & Digital Exhaust — typical feeds: Breach alerts (`breach:alert`), inbox stats (`inbox:stats`), cloud-drive usage (`clouddrive:usage`), certificate expiry (`certexpiry:check`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `backuprestore:test`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=backuprestore:test`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Personal cybersecurity feeds — Have-I-Been-Pwned breach alerts, personal email/inbox stats, cloud-storage usage APIs, and personal TLS-certificate expiry checks — sent to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs..

**Author notes:** Capture explicit outcome states for backup test restores events in `index=personal` and review both attempts and success percentage over time.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "backuprestore:test", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=backuprestore:test earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Backup Test Restore Success Rate** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=backuprestore:test`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `attempts` (> 0) after count — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `attempts`, `backup_set`, `success_pct`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=backuprestore:test
| bin _time span=1w
| stats count as attempts count(eval(status="success")) as successful by _time backup_set
| eval success_pct=if(attempts>0,round(100*successful/attempts,1),0)
| sort - _time
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=backuprestore:test earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, attempts, backup_set, success_pct
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=backuprestore:test earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `attempts` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=backuprestore:test earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(attempts) AS p50 perc90(attempts) AS p90 perc99(attempts) AS p99 max(attempts) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.38.22: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Time Chart Of Success Percentage For Backup Test Restores By Backup Set (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `backuprestore:test` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=backuprestore:test | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1w` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1w` buckets.
